children: The Indian rupee opened lower versus the US dollar on August 31, with the prospect of a Federal Reserve rate hike adding to headwinds from high oil prices, while bonds may see further selling pressure if economic growth strengthens.
The rupee opened lower by 10 paise at 95.48 per dollar, compared with Friday’s close of 95.38.
According to Finrex, the rupee is set to open about 19 paisa lower at 95.56 levels as dollar index rose to 99.66 while most other assets fell from their levels on Friday.

The rupee is expected to be in the range of 95.25 to 95.75 with exporters to sell near to 95.60 levels and importers to buy all dips that they get with no directional movement being seen in the currencies. Today is the last day for mobilization of deposits under RBIs FCNR (B) scheme, it added.

Asian currencies were mixed against the US dollar, with the Indonesian Rupiah gaining 0.29% and the Japanese Yen rising 0.09%. The South Korean Won slipped 0.04%, while the Philippines Peso declined 0.10%. The Thai Baht fell 0.19%, and the Taiwan Dollar weakened 0.17%. The China Renminbi eased 0.14%, while the Malaysian Ringgit dropped 0.20%. The Singapore Dollar also edged lower by 0.02%.

The dollar held steady near a two-week high on Monday as markets ramped up bets on a rate hike after hawkish remarks by Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh, while the yen slipped back through the closely watched 160-per-dollar level.

title: Currency Check: Rupee opens 10 paise lower at 95.48; Asian peers trade mostly lower
